target.title: fix: skip volatile backup cache paths
target.body:
Fixes #98865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw backup create` could still traverse disposable agent runtime caches, browser cache/resource-cache trees, retired archive copies, and state-side transient sidecars. Those paths can bloat archives or race with tar even though they have no restoration value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing backup archive path already centralizes volatile filtering through `isVolatileBackupPath`, so this extends that owner boundary instead of adding another archive-time special case. Browser filtering is intentionally scoped to cache-like directories under managed `user-data` paths so durable profile files such as `Preferences` and `Login Data` remain eligible for backup. `.lock` and `.partial` files are scoped to cache, queue, and tmp scratch roots so installed plugin source under `state/extensions` stays backed up; SQLite sidecars stay under the backup SQLite snapshot consistency guard instead of being treated as generic volatile files.

Issue #98865 was closed manually rather than by a merged runtime fix. I checked current `upstream/main`, the issue closure events, and related PR search; I found a docs-only open PR (#99007) but no equivalent runtime fix on main.

## User Impact

Backups now skip more disposable runtime/cache files and retired archive copies, reducing archive size and avoiding avoidable live-file races while preserving durable OpenClaw state, browser profile data, installed plugin source files, and SQLite consistency checks.

## Evidence

Current head: `80b7e213c41e7b2d2a24af70584489ef34c13bb8`.

Scope follow-up: this PR is now backup-only again. The unrelated QA-lab Crabline readiness timeout follow-up was removed from the branch so maintainers only need to review the backup archive payload boundary.

Claim proved: the backup path skips disposable cache/runtime/archive sidecars while preserving durable browser profile files, installed plugin files, and SQLite snapshot consistency behavior.

Focused current-head validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.test.ts`  
  Result: passed, 61 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-create.test.ts -- --testNamePattern "fails when SQLite-looking state appears after snapshot discovery|surfaces the volatile skip count in the summary"`  
  Result: passed, 3 tests, 36 skipped. This covers the CI failure where `late.sqlite-wal` must still trigger the SQLite snapshot retry error instead of being swallowed by the volatile filter, plus the volatile skip-count summary.
- `node_modules\.bin\oxlint.CMD src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.ts src/infra/backup-create.test.ts`  
  Result: passed.
- `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.ts src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.test.ts src/infra/backup-create.ts src/infra/backup-create.test.ts docs/cli/backup.md`  
  Result: passed.
- `git diff --check`  
  Result: passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`  
  Result: exited 0 with no actionable output.

Earlier real archive proof from the changed source path:

- Command: seeded a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, then ran `corepack pnpm openclaw backup create --output <temp>/backup-proof.tar.gz --no-include-workspace --json`.
- Result: the CLI completed successfully and returned `"skippedVolatileCount": 8`.
- Archive listing checks after `tar.t(...)`:
  - `OK ABSENT agents/main/agent/cache/provider.json`
  - `OK ABSENT agents/main/agent/shell-snapshots/bash.json`
  - `OK ABSENT cache/shell-snapshots/startup.json`
  - `OK ABSENT browser/openclaw/user-data/Default/Cache/data_0`
  - `OK ABSENT browser/openclaw/user-data/Default/Code Cache/js/index`
  - `OK ABSENT archived/old/openclaw-backup.tar.gz`
  - `OK ABSENT tmp/download.partial`
  - `OK ABSENT tmp/backup.lock`
  - `OK PRESENT browser/openclaw/user-data/Default/Preferences`
  - `OK PRESENT browser/openclaw/user-data/Default/Login Data`
  - `OK PRESENT extensions/demo/openclaw.plugin.json`
  - `OK PRESENT extensions/demo/bun.lock`
  - `OK PRESENT extensions/demo/download.partial`
  - `OK PRESENT locks/backup.lock`

Not tested / proof gaps: I did not force a live disappearing-file `ENOENT` race during tar traversal on the latest head; this PR proves the payload boundary with the real `openclaw backup create` path and keeps the existing tar retry behavior covered by focused tests.
